questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses they had to offer was crucial for my choice and the fact that the classes were in English made a huge difference, since classes in English in  Denmark are more limited in the fields that I wanted to explore

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Really easy. I was informed everything through outlook. And the staff was helpful

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The staff helped me get into my room and apartment. There was orientation staff to in the introduction week

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: They had a lot of different residences, but they were the one's picking the residence for me. and they made a great choice

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The had a meal plan, but there was a kitchen in the apartment, so the meal plan was not mandatory and you could cook yourself as I did. And it worked out great

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That it is better to live on campus than off. There are much more community and fun activities which are easy to get to because you live central. The residences themselves sometimes have some fun activities. And moreover, it is much more safe to live on campus than off.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You submit your courses and wait for them to be enrolled and approved. You can choose a lot of different courses and they urge you to pick more than the required in case there are some they do not approve. The process is very easy, but it takes a while to understand the system of courses, because they have some rules regarding inline courses and there are letters meaning different things etc, and there are some pre-requirements for courses also which you may not fulfil, so that part is more difficult.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could contact an email and they were quick to answer, but you cannot expect immediate answer and it will probably take some days.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got everything I wanted and they were flexible and helped with a few problems

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You will have to put in some time and effort, because it is not as easy as it sounds

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was good and I was able to follow along, but they require different things than in Denmark, so actually use your time on studies so you can get a good grade

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I loved that the final grade was sorted out to different areas, so that the final exam didn't count 100%. In that way you have time to experiment and fail, without it having to affect your whole grade. Because in UCPH if you have a bad day it's too damn bad

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved everything except for Speculative Fiction

questions.answer: The clubs were unexpected

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The academic books were really expensive and we had to get a lot more than what we would normally need in Copenhagen

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had a lot of different fields. All sports basically and hobbies you didn't even think of yourself. There was room for everyone

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The outdoor club is really nice and a way to explore parts of the city and outside of it without being on your own

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to nearby cities and book your bus tickets in advance just to be sure. I would not recommend a big travel unless it is in the break. It will be too stressful if you want to both travel a lot and be studying and meeting people at your university. You can always come back in the future and explore more of Canada

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, but the food was really bad. Idk what they put in it

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs and be open with your classmates. You can also attend the fun activities they do like HOCO and other stuff

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I something that was really different at that I didn't like was the food and that the main transportation was by car. It is not very student friendly and the public transport was bad and always late. So, it is really difficult to get around

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated the university and the people in it

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Be alert when going to town. There is a lot of homeless people and they can be very uncomfortable so keep and eye just in case
2) Join clubs -- people are really friendly and love exchange students. It is very easy to mingle 
3) Actually pick courses that you are interested in since you will be tested more frequently and will spend more time on it than you would think. So if you pick courses that you are not interested in it will affect your stay

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: When the weather-app says that it feels like -25 degrees is not that bad (only if it is very windy) It is to some extend colder in Denmark tbh

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships I made and courses I chose. I am more aware now of what kind of study I like

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The trip to get groceries. It is a long process with the public transport and the distance to get there. And their stores are huge so it takes some time compared to the quick trips to Netto

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
